title: Uniform measure of a set equals its relative cardinality
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty finite set, equipped with the uniform probability measure that assigns each point mass $1/\abs{\Omega}$, and let $S \subseteq \Omega$. Then the measure of $S$, as a real number, is
\[
  \frac{\abs{\{\omega \in \Omega \mid \omega \in S\}}}{\abs{\Omega}},
\]
the number of elements of $\Omega$ lying in $S$ divided by the total number of elements of $\Omega$.
hypotheses_covered: S is a subset of Ω
measure is the uniform probability measure on all of Ω
replaced:
Let $\Omega$ be a nonempty finite discrete type and let $S \subseteq \Omega$.  Under
the uniform probability measure on $\Omega$,
\[
  \bigl(\mathrm{uniformOn}\,\Omega\bigr)^{\mathbb{R}}(S)
  \;=\; \frac{\#\{\omega \in \Omega \mid \omega \in S\}}{|\Omega|}.
\]
